To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lifetime of the local vibrational modes of interstitial oxygen is determined by the activity of three phonon combinations and that the activity of these combinations in silicon and germania is significantly different.

(i) the vibrational lifetimes of interstitial oxygen isotopes in Si decrease with increasing isotope mass; (ii) the vibrational lifetime of the interstitial 16 O isotope in Ge is 125 ps, which is about an order of magnitude larger than the vibrational lifetime in Si; (iii) the vibrational dynamics of interstitial oxygen are governed by anharmonic coupling to phonons.

the lifetimes of local vibrations of interstitial oxygen isotopes are shorter than the lifetimes of bulk vibrations by a factor of approximately 100 and are determined by the density of the phonon combinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between local modes and phonon bath in Si and Ge.
the interaction between the local vibrational modes of interstitial oxygen atoms in silicon and germanum and the lattice vibrations.
the decay of the asymmetric stretching mode of the interstitial oxygen in germanium and silicon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lifetimes of interstitial oxygen modes in Si are determined by three phonon decay processes, whereas the lifetime in Ge is determined by two phonon decay processes.
the decay of the interstitial oxygen local mode in Si and Ge is determined by the interaction with the highest density of states of the lattice phonons.
the lifetimes of oxygen interstitials are governed by the phonon density at the frequency of the local mode and the strength of the local mode-phonon interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vibrational lifetimes of interstitial oxygen isotopes in Si and Ge are strongly influenced by the activity of the lattice vibrations in the vicinity of the local mode frequencies.
the vibrational lifetimes are strongly influenced by the local phonon density of the lattice.

the decay of the local modes in Si is faster than that in Ge, which is in line with the faster decay of the interstitial 16 O mode in Si compared to the 17O one.
